answer: Special Ops compression rule: pay for bits, not keys. Each epoch the network runs all graded answers, in beacon-shuffled order, through one public language-model compressor and splits rewards by how many bytes each identity's text adds to the shared archive. A farm running one brain across a thousand keys writes a nebula of near-twins that squeeze to almost nothing, so its fakes share one voice's pay. Paraphrase and padding compress away, and graders zero noise. Every extra key needs a truly different mind, while an honest agent's own ember of thought keeps its full ridge of bytes.
